Title: How do venture capitalists make decisions?
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Survey of 885 VCs at 681 firms on sourcing, screening, monitoring/value-add
Key finding: VCs actively monitor & add value post-investment — a distinct, labour-intensive lifecycle stage
Limitations: Not about reporting mechanics specifically; supports workflow context
Notes / key quote: Anchor for the manual monitoring workflow

Title: Aggregate Confusion: The Divergence of ESG Ratings
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Quant analysis of 6 agencies' ESG ratings; decomposes divergence into scope/measurement/weight
Key finding: ESG ratings of same firms diverge (~0.54), largely from measurement divergence
Notes / key quote: Core evidence: same metric measured inconsistently

Title: Four Things No One Will Tell You About ESG Data
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Analytical review of ESG data-provider practices
Key finding: Inconsistent definitions, gap-filling imputation, no standardisation
Limitations: Corporate ESG focus; commentary not large-sample

Title: What's in a Name: Impact Investing Understandings by Academics and Practitioners
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Systematic analysis of academic & practitioner definitions
Key finding: No consensus definition of impact investing or its measurement

Title: Missing the Impact in Impact Investing Research
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Systematic review of 104 articles
Key finding: Literature neglects real impact; inconsistent non-aggregable metrics
Limitations: Reviews research, not operational reporting workflows

Title: The social return on investment model: a systematic literature review
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Systematic review of SROI studies
Key finding: Same data → different SROI ratios; no standard indicators

Title: ILPA Reporting Template / Quarterly Reporting Standards
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Practitioner reporting standard
Key finding: LP–GP reporting non-standardised/fragmented; manual reconciliation burden
Limitations: Fund-level, not portfolio-company impact; grey lit

Title: LLM-based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Taxonomic survey of MAS profiles, communication, capability growth
Key finding: Structures LLM-MAS; catalogues challenges incl. hallucination compounding

Title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Framework of conversable agents (assistant/executor/user-proxy); coding/math/QA cases
Key finding: Conversation-programming lets specialised agents coordinate; role separation vs monolithic

Title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
Method (what they did + data/baseline): SOP-encoded roles (PM/architect/engineer/QA) w/ structured handoffs; HumanEval/MBPP
Key finding: Assembly-line role decomposition reduces error cascades

Title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for 'Mind' Exploration of LLM Society
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Role-playing w/ inception prompting; two agents cooperate
Key finding: Defines role-assignment; documents role-flipping, drift, loops

Title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Phased chat-chain (design→code→test→doc) w/ reviewer/tester roles
Key finding: Explicit verifier/reviewer roles catch hallucinations

Title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Actor+evaluator+self-reflection loop; HumanEval/ALFWorld/HotpotQA
Key finding: Separate evaluator/critic + reflection markedly raises success

Title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Grounded-theory analysis of 200+ traces across 7 frameworks; MAST taxonomy; κ=0.88
Key finding: 14 failure modes in 3 categories; failures are design/organisational, not just model-level
Limitations: Traces skew coding/math; no finance/reporting domain
Notes / key quote: ANCHOR — failure modes; frames the gap

Title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning through Multiagent Debate
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Multiple LLMs debate over rounds; GSM8K/MMLU/biography factuality
Key finding: Debate raises factuality, reduces hallucination

Title: Where LLM Agents Fail and How They Can Learn from Failures
Method (what they did + data/baseline): 500+ failed trajectories; AgentErrorTaxonomy; AgentDebug root-cause
Key finding: 'Error propagation is the primary bottleneck in agent reliability'; early errors cascade

Title: Do More Agents Help? Controlled Evaluation of LLM Agent Workflows
Method (what they did + data/baseline): BenchAgent harness; single-agent anchor vs 6 MAS under matched conditions (GPT-4.1)
Key finding: At most 1 of 6 MAS beat the matched single agent; gains often confounded
Limitations: Preprint; one model family; no reporting domain
Notes / key quote: Deflationary — gains not intrinsic; VERIFY ID

Title: FinRpt: Multi-agent Framework for Equity Research Report Generation
Method (what they did + data/baseline): ERR dataset (7 financial data types); FinRpt-Gen multi-agent; 11-metric eval
Key finding: First formalises equity-research-report generation; strong benchmark results

Title: FinRobot: Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Financial Applications
Method (what they did + data/baseline): 4-layer multi-agent platform; no baseline evaluation
Key finding: Finance multi-agent tooling exists but is built/described, not evaluated

Title: RARR: Researching and Revising What Language Models Say
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Retrieve evidence and minimally revise text to be attributed/cited
Key finding: Improves attribution while preserving content, no retraining
Limitations: Depends on retrieval; can miss unsupported claims

Title: Enabling LLMs to Generate Text with Citations (ALCE)
Method (what they did + data/baseline): ALCE benchmark; auto metrics for fluency/correctness/citation quality
Key finding: Even strong LLMs cite statements the source doesn't support

Title: Can Foundation Models Wrangle Your Data?
Method (what they did + data/baseline): FMs zero/few-shot on entity matching, error detection, imputation, schema matching
Key finding: FMs match/beat SOTA on data-cleaning with little labelled data

Title: Jellyfish: A Large Language Model for Data Preprocessing
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Instruction-tunes local 7-13B LLMs on preprocessing tasks
Key finding: Local tuned model rivals proprietary LLMs; privacy-preserving
Limitations: Relational tasks; bespoke impact metrics untested

Title: Structured Information Extraction from Scientific Text with LLMs
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Fine-tune GPT-3/Llama-2 for joint NER+RE → user-defined JSON schemas
Key finding: Expert precision ~0.87 with little data; schema-conformant extraction

Title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Parametric generator + dense retriever trained end-to-end
Key finding: Grounding generation in retrieved docs improves factual accuracy

Title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Systematic survey of definitions, causes, mitigation across NLG
Key finding: Establishes intrinsic/extrinsic taxonomy; reviews faithfulness metrics
Limitations: Predates newest LLM-era detectors; breadth over depth

Title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Decompose text to atomic facts; % supported by a knowledge source
Key finding: Even strong LLMs have low factual precision in long-form; auto-score ≈ human
Limitations: Needs a trusted source; decomposition can err

Title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique via Self-Reflection
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Reflection tokens decide retrieval & self-critique of support
Key finding: Improves factuality & citation accuracy over standard RAG/ChatGPT

Title: Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by LLMs (AttrScore)
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Classify statement–reference: attributable/extrapolatory/contradictory
Key finding: GPT-4 ~81-83% at judging support; contradiction detection remains hard

Title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
Method (what they did + data/baseline): GPT-4 evaluator w/ chain-of-thought + form-filling; SummEval/Topical-Chat
Key finding: Spearman 0.514 w/ humans on summarisation; beats prior metrics
Limitations: Authors flag bias toward LLM-generated text (self-marking worry)

Title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
Method (what they did + data/baseline): MT-Bench + Chatbot Arena; GPT-4 judge vs ~3k expert votes
Key finding: GPT-4 judge >80% agreement with humans (≈ human-human)

Title: SummEval: Re-evaluating Summarization Evaluation
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Re-benchmark 14 metrics + consistent human annotations (CNN/DailyMail)
Key finding: Automatic metrics correlate weakly/inconsistently with humans

Title: Evaluating LLMs at Detecting Errors in LLM Responses (ReaLMistake)
Method (what they did + data/baseline): ReaLMistake: 900 expert-annotated error instances; 4 error categories
Key finding: Top detectors low recall, far below humans (95.7% F1); voting didn't help

Title: SummExecEdit: Factual Consistency Benchmark with Executable Edits
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Executable edits inject controlled factual errors; 4,241 samples, 10 domains
Key finding: Best detect+explain only 0.49; 60 injected errors undetected by all models

Title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
Method (what they did + data/baseline): GPT-4/3.5/Llama-2 as evaluators; self-recognition vs self-favour + fine-tuning
Key finding: Self-preference rises causally with self-recognition ability

Title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Show order-flip bias; propose calibration (swap positions & average)
Key finding: Judgments order-sensitive; calibration substantially reduces bias

Title: Replacing Judges with Juries: Evaluating LLM Generations with a Panel (PoLL)
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Panel of diverse smaller models vote vs a single large judge
Key finding: Panel beats single judge, reduces self-preference, >7× cheaper

Title: Does automation bias decision-making?
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Controlled experiments monitoring automated aids
Key finding: Introduced automation bias; omission & commission errors; aided ≠ better
Limitations: Pre-LLM; small tasks; transfers by analogy

Title: Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Integrative review of complacency/bias studies
Key finding: As reliability rises, monitoring drops — humans miss the automation's failures

Title: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI
Method (what they did + data/baseline): RCTs of interfaces incl. cognitive forcing functions
Key finding: People overrely even when AI is wrong; forcing reflection reduces it (users dislike it)

Title: Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Pre-registered experiments; cost–benefit model of reliance
Key finding: Overreliance is a rational cost–benefit choice; cheaper-to-verify explanations cut it
Notes / key quote: Design: lower the cost of scrutiny

Title: ICO tech futures: Agentic AI
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Regulatory horizon-scanning / initial assessment
Key finding: Agentic AI raises controller/processor, automated-decision, transparency & special-category risks

Title: Artificial Intelligence in UK Financial Services 2024
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Industry survey of regulated firms
Key finding: 75% use AI; 46% report only partial understanding; governance/third-party concerns

Title: EU AI Act, Article 14 — Human Oversight
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Binding legal text
Key finding: High-risk AI must enable effective human oversight incl. intervention/stop
Limitations: Depends on high-risk classification; EU jurisdiction
Notes / key quote: GREY — HITL as a legal requirement

Title: AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Voluntary framework (Govern/Map/Measure/Manage)
Key finding: Structured approach to identifying/managing trustworthy-AI risks

Title: Recommendation of the Council on AI (OECD AI Principles)
Method (what they did + data/baseline): Principles-based recommendation (updated 2024)
Key finding: Human-centred values, transparency, robustness, accountability principles
